extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners conducting scoping/systematic reviews of sport-related concussion policy and guidelines (public health, sports-medicine, policy analysts)
extracted.subtask_description: A PRISMA-ScR scoping review protocol to map literature on sport-related concussion (SRC) policies, protocols, and suggested guidelines across sports settings, identifying components, variations, and opportunities for standardisation. The record is an OSF-registered review with open-license metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PRISMA-ScR methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: This PRISMA scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) seeks to map the breadth of existing literature on SRC policies, protocols, and suggested guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied requirement to follow PRISMA-ScR reporting and methodological standards for scoping reviews (i.e., structured, transparent mapping rather than a quantitative meta-analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include both academic and grey literature
rubrics_metrics.description: This review includes both academic and grey literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search strategy and inclusion must capture peer-reviewed studies and non-peer-reviewed sources (e.g., policy documents, organizational guidelines) to comprehensively map available SRC policy/protocol material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility focused on sources containing SRC policy/guidelines/protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility criteria focusing on sources that include SRC policy, guidelines, and protocols in sports and athletics environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only sources that contain explicit policy, protocol, or suggested guideline content related to sport-related concussion in athletic settings qualify for inclusion; purely observational or unrelated clinical studies without policy/guideline content should be excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map key components, variations, and opportunities for standardisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify key components, variations, and opportunities for standardisation in concussion management across various sports settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extraction and synthesis should catalogue constituent elements of policies/protocols (e.g., definitions, diagnostic criteria, return-to-play procedures), note differences across documents/contexts, and highlight areas amenable to harmonisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess inconsistencies in definitions, diagnostic criteria, and management strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Despite increasing awareness of SRC, inconsistencies persist in definitions, diagnostic criteria, and management strategies across different sports and regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis should explicitly compare and report on terminological, diagnostic, and management divergences across sports/regions and consider implications for practice and policy coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on athletic population impacts and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Sport-related concussions (SRC) are a major health concern due to their high prevalence, unique individualistic nature, and potential chronic health impacts in the athletic population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing of the review and interpretation of findings should consider prevalence, individual variability, and potential long-term harms when evaluating the adequacy and aims of policies/protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open registration and licensing / transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: OSF registration with DOI (10.17605/OSF.IO/VKJEN) and CC BY 4.0 license are associated with the item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocol transparency (public registration, persistent identifier) and open licensing are treated as part of good-practice standards for review reporting and reproducibility.
